label: prop:ground-state-ordering
title: The interleaved ordering does not minimise the dilogarithm volume
html:
Proposition. The interleaved ordering does not minimise the dilogarithm volume

Proposition (negative). Let Z protons and N neutrons (A = Z + N) be arranged along the transfer-matrix chain, and let

  \Phi_q = \sum_i \log|\hat{V}_i|

be the quantum dilogarithm volume of that chain. Consider the interleaved, tail-packed arrangement

  \mathrm{ordering}[k]
  =
  \begin{cases}
    1 \text{ (proton)} & k \text{ odd}, \; k < 2Z \\
    0 \text{ (neutron)} & \text{otherwise.}
  \end{cases}

This arrangement does not minimise \Phi_q. Explicitly, at A = 5, Z = 1, N = 4 it is the strict maximiser: the sorted arrangement p\,n\,n\,n\,n satisfies

  \Phi_q(p\,n\,n\,n\,n) < \Phi_q(n\,p\,n\,n\,n)

for every q in an interval containing the substrate anchor q_0 \approx 1.10998 and for every Markov parameter lying strictly between the two transfer-matrix eigenvalues, with equality only in the undeformed limit q \to 1.

The eigenvalue relation \lambda_+\lambda_- = -1 for the transfer matrix survives; the ordering claim does not.

Status of the three rules

The proposition previously asserted three rules. An exhaustive sweep of \Phi_q over every \binom{A}{Z} arrangement for A \leq 16, at the experimental (proton) anchor, settles each of them.

(i) Interleaving — refuted for A \geq 4. The interleaved arrangement is the \Phi_q minimiser in 17 of 62 swept cases on the bare-nucleon readout (10 of 62 with the electron tail), and is the strict maximiser in 12 (respectively 8). It is not the ground state.

(ii) Tail packing — refuted. The minimising arrangement head-packs, not tail-packs. At Z = 1 the minimising proton position is A - 5 for every 6 \leq N \leq 15, leaving exactly four neutrons after it and all remaining neutrons before it. For Z \geq 2 the minimiser is an interleaved block at an interior offset with neutron runs on both sides.

(iii) Boundary correction (A \leq 3) — holds at A = 3, fails as stated at A = 2. At A = 3 the sorted arrangement is the exhaustive minimiser, on both readouts and on both sides of Z \leq N. At A = 2 the two arrangements are exactly degenerate on the bare chain — a consequence of the transfer factors commuting, so that the readout sees the crossing coefficients only as a multiset — so sorted does not beat interleaving; and with the electron tail appended, sorted is strictly the worse of the two.

Two readouts, not one

\Phi_q is computed in two inequivalent ways in the corpus: over the bare nucleon chain, and over the nucleon chain with an electron tail appended. The verdicts above are stated for both. They differ only for rule (iii) at A = 2, a case that the production path special-cases and never routes through the ordering at all.

The readout as a two-parameter object

Each transfer factor is T(d) = S + d\,\mathbf{1} for a single fixed matrix S with \mathrm{tr}\, S = q - q^{-1} and \det S = -1. All such factors commute, so the chain product depends on the crossing coefficients only as a multiset, and S^2 = (q-q^{-1})S + \mathbf{1} collapses the product to \alpha\mathbf{1} + \beta S. The vertex volume is therefore

  \hat{V}_i = c_+\mu_+ + c_-\mu_-,
  \qquad
  \mu_\pm = \prod_{j > i}(\lambda_\pm + d_{ij}),

with \lambda_+ = q, \lambda_- = -q^{-1} the roots of the characteristic polynomial and, writing z for the Markov parameter,

  c_+ = \frac{z + q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}},
  \qquad
  c_- = \frac{q - z}{q + q^{-1}},
  \qquad
  c_+ + c_- = 1 .

The sum is 1 identically in z, and z enters the readout nowhere else.

Independence of the Markov-parameter convention

The two arrangements differ at positions 0 and 1 only, and that comparison collapses to a single identity in which z survives only inside the product c_+c_-:

  \hat{V}_0\hat{V}_1(n\,p\,n\,n\,n) - \hat{V}_0\hat{V}_1(p\,n\,n\,n\,n)
  = 2\,c_+c_-\left(\frac{q + q^{-1}}{2}\right)^{4}\frac{q^6 - 1}{q^3},
  \qquad
  4\,c_+c_- = \frac{4q\,(q - z)(qz + 1)}{(q^2 + 1)^2},

the fourth power being the mixed proton–neutron eigenfactor, which carries no z. For q > 1 every other factor is positive, so the counterexample holds exactly when -q^{-1} < z < q — the Markov parameter strictly between the two eigenvalues. Both the canonical convention D, z = q^3/(q^2+1), and the excised convention C, z = \sqrt{q}/(q+1), lie in that window for every q > 1, so the refutation is a fact about the readout rather than about a choice of z; it degenerates to equality only at q = 1, where the deformation switches off, which is why it holds on a whole interval rather than at a single anchor.

Scope

The A \geq 4 refutation is a structural exclusion: an explicit arrangement with strictly smaller \Phi_q, proved for an interval of q containing the anchor and for every Markov parameter in the window above. The description of the actual minimising family is empirical, covering A \leq 16 only, and no claim is made beyond that range. Which ordering the mass and binding computations should use is a separate question and is not settled here.
